cli.nestedSkillInvocation: Kimi built-in Skill tool with { skill, args }; never literal /skill text

stableEngineEnv.KIMI_MODEL_THINKING_EFFORT: low|high|max only for kimi-code/k3; omitted K3 effort preserves Kimi's documented high default; unset for every other model

cli.windowsPromptTransport: For the standard npm kimi.cmd/bat shim, prompt bytes travel over stdin to a fixed Node bootstrap which restores process.argv before importing Kimi; native executables fail above a 30000 UTF-16 command-line budget.
cli.initialActivationTelemetry: Visible prompt parity only; the external materializer cannot emit Kimi-private skill.activated/origin telemetry.
cli.cancellation: The runner forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP to its direct Kimi child; the embedding host remains responsible for platform process-tree teardown.
cli.notes: CLI-only provider execution. Installation uses the deterministic Core CLI above. Headless workflows use the managed Node skill runner, never literal /skill text in kimi -p. Authenticate once with kimi login.

standard.description: Deterministic installation of the provider workflows and required skills. Roles are defined by the programmatic runtime; no role file is installed. No model invocation or enrichment.

fields.tier: Deprecated legacy string, tolerated and ignored; all installs use deterministic placement.
fields.agents: Optional, deprecated since Core 6.3: roles are runtime-defined, so the section has no effect on the installed artifacts. Validated for shape when present; a non-empty agents.selected logs a deprecation warning.
fields.agents.selected: string[] — optional, deprecated: unique lowercase kebab-case agent ids (1-64 characters), accepted and ignored
fields.agents.excluded: string[] — optional, deprecated: unique lowercase kebab-case agent ids; must not overlap agents.selected
fields.models.preset: string — balanced | budget | max; resolved within the selected provider catalog
fields.models.defaults.model: string — exact provider model id or configured alias (overrides preset; Kimi: 1-128 characters matching [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/:-]*; default: k3)
fields.models.overrides: Record<safe-agent-id, string> — exact per-agent provider model ids or configured aliases with the same provider-specific validation (highest priority)

checkpoints.base_install: Runtime prerequisites and artifact workspace resolved
checkpoints.command_generation: Workflow commands, required skills and installation manifest verified

balanced.description: Legacy Claude preset view retained for existing consumers. Other providers resolve this preset through providerModelCatalogs.

budget.description: Legacy Claude preset view retained for existing consumers. Other providers resolve this preset through providerModelCatalogs.

max.description: Legacy Claude preset view retained for existing consumers. Other providers resolve this preset through providerModelCatalogs.

kimi.note: Install config retains exact ids or safe custom aliases. Preset names do not imply Claude aliases for Kimi. Process launch prefixes only the three documented official short ids with kimi-code/; every custom alias that matches the published model grammar passes through unchanged.

legacyCompat.note: Core installs directly and is driven by Desktop through init and the offline framework lifecycle (install-framework, swap-current, assemble). enrich, update, doctor, profile, --quick and --lite are removed.

agentRuntime.checkpointEnvelope: checkpoint.json holds {format: 2, checksum, state, graph}: the host ledger (state) and the LangGraph checkpoint history (graph) written atomically together
agentRuntime.apiOperation: runtime api emits {type: runtime-api, apiVersion, coreVersion, runtimeIdentity, workflowVersions, engineVersion, engines, nodeKindsVersion, nodeKinds, capabilities, guardrails}; does not invoke providers
agentRuntime.validationTransport: runtime validate --stdin accepts UTF-8 configuration JSON up to 2 MiB, mutually exclusive with --config
agentRuntime.compactStatus: runtime status --compact omits workflow history, events and outputs, frozen pipeline context and verification command output; retains identities (runId, traceId), phase statuses and visits, pendingApproval, pendingQuestion, usage, completion, acceptance summary and verification metadata
agentRuntime.interrupts: A paused run (exit 2) carries pendingApproval (resume --approve <step>) or pendingQuestion (resume --answer <text>, nonempty, at most 20000 characters); the architect asks only after one autonomous investigation pass unless architect.onLowConfidence is proceed
agentRuntime.eventStream: run/resume emit JSON lines typed workflow-event, agent-event, verification-output, span ({traceId, spanId, name, stepId, attempt, visit, startedAt, endedAt, status, usage?, error?}) and a final runtime-result
agentRuntime.reviewGate: review.minScore and review.aspects may only tighten Core's own gate (minScore 70, security 75, other aspects 60); the pipeline journal enforces the floor
agentRuntime.acceptance: The reviewer certifies every frozen acceptance criterion by specId and criterionIndex; Core records the verification commands it ran as required checks and binds the report to the exact candidate before the reviewer verdict

reviewBrief.advisory: The reviewer's optional risk brief never changes the approval gate
reviewBrief.runResult: runtime-result.reviewBrief: {schemaVersion: 1, change, approved, score, recordedAt, brief | null, diagnostic?} | null (engine 1 builtin runs)
reviewBrief.confidenceScore: openspec/changes/<change>/confidence-score.json brief (approved verdicts; archived with the change)
reviewBrief.stepOutput: reviewer step output brief / briefDiagnostic; engine 2 implementation output review.brief

architectClarifications.output: architect reply clarifications: [{question, impact: high|medium|low, default: string | null}] (at most 5) before planning
architectClarifications.pause: ask-on-high and a high-impact clarification with default null pauses the run with pendingQuestion (the questions, numbered when several); resume --answer feeds the answer to the architect as authoritative
architectClarifications.proceed: otherwise the architect plans on its defaults and records them under Assumptions in design.md
architectClarifications.designSections: design.md must contain a non-empty Non-Goals section (and Assumptions when clarifications were listed); a missing section spends the architect's single repair turn
architectClarifications.runResult: runtime-result.clarifications: {schemaVersion: 1, change, policy, status: awaiting-answers | proceeded, recordedAt, clarifications, blocking, answers, assumptions} | null (engine 1 builtin runs)
architectClarifications.stepOutput: architect step output clarifications; graph state architecture.clarifications

specTrace.requirementId: <capability>/<slug> from '### Requirement: <name>' in openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md (and the change's ADDED/MODIFIED/RENAMED deltas); slug: NFKD without accents, lowercase, every run of non-alphanumerics one '-', no leading or trailing '-'
specTrace.testTags: [spec:<capability>/<slug>] in a test title, or a '// spec: <capability>/<slug>' comment ('# spec:' for Python and shell) on the line before the test; any language
specTrace.states: demonstrated: tagged test file reached by a verification command that exited 0; undemonstrated: reason no-test | not-executed | failed; untagged: tags that match no requirement (advisory)
specTrace.report: {schemaVersion: 1, generatedAt, changes, evidence: receipt | tests-passed | none, receiptId, requirements, demonstrated[{id, name, tests}], undemonstrated[{id, name, reason, tests}], untagged[{tag, repositoryId, file, line, form}], touched, touchedUndemonstrated, scannedFiles}
specTrace.reportPath: <backlogRoot>/.specrails/pipeline/<runId>/spec-trace.json (written after each passing verification, bound to the receipt id)
specTrace.runResult: runtime-result.specTrace: the report | null (engine 1 builtin runs)
specTrace.advisory: The trace never changes verification or acceptance status; the acceptance report carries a finding 'Spec trace (advisory, receipt <id>): Requirements demonstrated X/Y…', the reviewer treats a touched requirement without a demonstrated tag as an issue
specTrace.divergences: reviewer check 9 fills brief.divergences[{capability, requirement, observed}] with spec claims of touched capabilities the code contradicts
specTrace.cli: specrails-core pipeline trace [--root <dir>] [--context <context.json>] [--change <name>[,...]] [--tests <glob>[,...]] [--tests-passed] [--check] [--json] [--out <file>]; installed projects also get node .specrails/runtime/trace.mjs; normal mode exits 0, --check exits 1 when a requirement touched by the change is not demonstrated
specTrace.driftSweepDefinition: src/agent-runtime/engine/__fixtures__/drift-sweep.json (read-only role-turn of a host-declared read role drift-auditor; structured output {divergences[{capability, requirement, observed}], unchecked[]})

baselineOnTouch.capabilityMap: openspec/capability-map.json {schemaVersion: 1, capabilities: {<capability>: {files: string[], changes: string[]}}}; the archive step merges the files each archived change touched into every capability of its delta specs (paths prefixed '<repositoryId>:' outside the artifact repository); excluded from the reviewed candidate
baselineOnTouch.detection: after planning, design.md Blast radius files that exist, are code (not tests, docs or lockfiles) and appear neither in the capability map nor as a path or specific directory in openspec/specs are uncovered
baselineOnTouch.plan: uncovered files make the architect add a '## 0. Baseline' task group (characterization tests of current behaviour plus a minimal as-built spec under ADDED Requirements, requirements tagged per specTrace) in the same session
baselineOnTouch.hardRule: the developer's first turn writes only the Baseline group; Core refuses non-test edits and runs the verification plan on the unchanged code; failure stops the run (status blocked, error code baseline_characterization_failed) before the developer touches the module
baselineOnTouch.recordPath: <backlogRoot>/.specrails/pipeline/<runId>/baseline.json {schemaVersion: 1, change, status: not-needed | planned | passed | failed | violated, recordedAt, detection {blastRadius, covered, uncovered, skipped}, tests, receiptId?, reason?}
baselineOnTouch.runResult: runtime-result.baseline: the record | null (engine 1 builtin runs)
baselineOnTouch.cost: baseline turns run with invocation kind 'baseline'; efficiencySummary.invocations.byKind.baseline and efficiencySummary.baseline {invocations, roles, costUsd, inputTokens, outputTokens} keep their spend apart

rulesInventory.cli: specrails-core rules inventory [--root <repo>] [--artifact-root <dir>] [--offline] [--reclassify] [--json]; exits 0 and always writes the inventory (classification problems are reported in classification.status); init runs it offline after installing
rulesInventory.path: <artifactRoot>/.specrails/rules.json (the directory that holds .specrails/agent-runtime.json); the runtime reads <backlogRoot>/.specrails/rules.json, then <artifactRoot>/.specrails/rules.json
rulesInventory.schema: {schemaVersion: 1, generatedAt, gates[{id, kind: lint | format | typecheck | test | architecture | hook | ci | spec, command, source}], rules[{id, text, source: '<file>:<line>', status: enforcedBy | automatable | humanOnly | unclassified, enforcedBy?, proposedCheck?}], classification {status: classified | cached | offline | unavailable | failed | empty, provider?, model?, reason?, classifiedAt?, usage?}}
rulesInventory.gates: deterministic discovery in the repository: package scripts (lint, format, typecheck, test, architecture, openspec), lint/format configs (ESLint, Biome, Prettier, Ruff, Black, mypy, golangci-lint, rustfmt, clippy, RuboCop), tsconfig strict, architecture tests and dependency-cruiser, git hooks (.husky, .githooks, pre-commit, lefthook), check-like run steps of .github/workflows, openspec validate
rulesInventory.rules: list items and strongly normative sentences of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (also .github/ and docs/), outside code fences, tables and specrails-managed blocks; at most 200; id r-<12 hex> = hash of file and statement, stable across line moves
rulesInventory.classification: one provider call (agents.architect of .specrails/agent-runtime.json, read-only, no role instructions) classifies only rules without a cached classification; the model never adds, drops or rewrites a statement; offline, without configuration or on failure the rules stay unclassified
rulesInventory.reviewer: humanOnly rules are listed to the reviewer, who copies the ones the change could break into brief.humanChecks
rulesInventory.verification: with no host verification configured, the architect is offered the discovered gate commands as the default verification proposal for the artifact repository
rulesInventory.claudeInstructions: Claude Code installs get the sentinel-managed block (<!-- specrails-managed:start/end -->) in the root CLAUDE.md, like codex AGENTS.md, gemini GEMINI.md and kimi .kimi-code/AGENTS.md

failureClassification.record: {kind, phase?, rounds?, resetAt?, detail?, resumablePhase?, confidence: high | low}
failureClassification.runResult: runtime-result.failure and runtime-status.failure (both engines): the record when the run status is failed or blocked; absent otherwise. A run Core could not start (fatal argument or configuration error) carries none.
failureClassification.semantics: classified only from signals the run already produced (status, the failing step or node, error codes and messages); a failure it cannot tie to a documented signal is kind unknown with confidence low and a host must show it as an unknown cause. phase is the failing step id (engine 1) or node path (engine 2); rounds counts visits of correction steps; resetAt is the provider's own wording of the reset time, never reformatted; detail is one bounded sentence from the run's own error; resumablePhase is the step runtime resume continues from when resuming can help (blocked runs and transient kinds), absent for a plain failed verification.

kindMeaning.tests_failed: verification kept failing, or the correction loop stopped on the same failing change
kindMeaning.provider_limit: the provider reported a session, usage, rate or quota limit
kindMeaning.environment: the host environment cannot run verification (credentials, toolchain, setup command, non-deterministic generated output, edits outside the scope)
kindMeaning.blocked: a configured limit stopped the run: baseline characterization, attempt or budget limits, a reviewer rejecting the same change
kindMeaning.timeout: the total execution or active-duration limit elapsed
kindMeaning.tool_inactivity: the agent produced no tool call, reply or usage within the idle limit
kindMeaning.crash: the provider process, endpoint, lease or storage failed under the run

failureClassification.compatibility: additive: hosts ignore an absent field; an older Core never emits it and the host derives a low-confidence diagnosis from the error text

findingLocations.location: state.json acceptance.findingLocations in the run's pipeline directory, next to acceptance.findings (which stays string[])
findingLocations.semantics: finding is the zero-based index into acceptance.findings; path is repository-relative with forward slashes (never absolute, never containing ..); line and endLine are 1-based and optional (endLine only with line, greater than it). Core drops a malformed anchor instead of failing the review, keeps at most 50 and one per finding, and never invents a location: a finding without an entry is unanchored.
findingLocations.compatibility: additive: hosts ignore an absent field and render the finding unanchored; an older Core never emits it

pauseRuns.cli: specrails-core runtime pause --context <json> | --run-dir <dir> [--request-id <id>] [--reason <token>]; engine 2 runs only; always exits 0 with one line {type: runtime-pause-result, runId, requestId, reason, outcome, status, createdAt?}
pauseRuns.reason: lowercase token matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$, default requested (Desktop's daily budget guard sends budget)
pauseRuns.semantics: requested: the run executes under a live lease; the idempotent inbox request (same request id and reason returns the original record, a different reason is control_conflict) lets every admitted attempt finish and commit, refuses the next admission, settles status paused and releases the lease (the run process exits 2). paused: an ownerless run still marked running is settled paused directly. already-paused, not-running (failed, interrupted, blocked) and terminal (succeeded, cancelled, completed) change nothing. A run of another Core package is refused with resume_incompatible.
pauseRuns.status: runtime status and runtime-result state.pause {requestId, reason, at} while a requested pause holds the run (no pendingInterrupts); events pause_requested {requestId, reason} and workflow_paused {requestId, reason}
pauseRuns.resume: runtime resume continues a paused run from its last committed step without repeating it and discards pause requests that arrived before the resume

agentRuntime.programmaticRegistration: ExecutorRegistry.register(id, executor); custom executors implement AgentExecutor.execute(request)
agentRuntime.recovery: Explicit resume uses frozen configuration and revalidates Core evidence; interrupted writes require named recovery; grants persist until evidence invalidation.
agentRuntime.delivery: Core implements through archive; the host owns worktrees, commits, pushes, PRs and backlog delivery. A standalone continuation does not restart Desktop delivery.
agentRuntime.specificationFormat: Architect specs are OpenSpec delta specs authored through the official fast-forward skill (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED requirements); existing requirements are preserved through delta semantics and merged into main specs by OpenSpec archive. Complete replacement specs are not fabricated.
agentRuntime.compatibility: Additive to integration schema 4 and execution context schema 1. Legacy workflows and profile v1 remain supported. Hosts must check RUNTIME_API_VERSION, not infer runtime support from Core major version.

implementationSteps.ownership: Host definitions compose phases and freeze role definitions; Core executes individual operations and evidence gates

agentRuntime.frozenRequest: agent-runtime-request.json carries workflow {id, version, source: builtin|definition, definitionHash, engine: 1|2}; resume and status select the engine from workflow.engine and a request without the block is a legacy (engine 1) run
agentRuntime.developerTools: The developer role runs with each CLI's autonomous edit+shell mode (claude --tools default --dangerously-skip-permissions with Agent/Task/Skill disallowed; codex workspace-write; gemini --yolo; kimi print mode). Architect and reviewer stay read-only. Claude roles load project settings only (--setting-sources project,local).
agentRuntime.verificationPolicy: Configured commands are optional. The architect proposes commands for repositories without one; repositories with no automated check are admitted and recorded in the receipt as unverifiedRepositories. Unchecked tasks return to the developer as feedback instead of failing the run.
agentRuntime.sessionReuse: Developer correction passes resume the previous provider session (claude --resume, codex exec resume, gemini --resume, kimi --session) with a short correction prompt; an unavailable session falls back to a fresh full turn. Structured roles get one repair turn in-session when their JSON is unusable.
agentRuntime.structuredOutput: Claude receives --json-schema and Codex --output-schema for architect/reviewer replies; other providers are parsed leniently.
agentRuntime.resumeBudget: An explicit resume resets the transition ceiling and grants the developer a fresh maxAttempts budget.

deriveChange.roleAssignment: Core engine role: access read, artifacts all, openspecSkill openspec-ff-change; takes agents.architect's provider assignment; instructions are Core's and the id is reserved for custom roles

params.change: required; the run's frozen change name ({{run.changeId}})
params.summaryPath: optional; file relative to <backlogRoot>/.specrails/pipeline/<runId>/, at most 32768 bytes, no symlinks or .. segments; absent or empty derives from the diff alone; optional front matter 'transcriptTurns: <n>'
params.feedback: optional string (at most 32000 characters, normally {{run.latestFindings}}); when non-blank the deriver re-derives the existing change in place after a correction round, with the findings bounded to 8000 characters as untrusted fenced data under '## Re-derivation after a correction round'

deriveChange.diff: change-scope changeSet: repositories[].baseSha (or HEAD at first measurement) to the working tree; untracked files present at the first measurement are pre-existing; .specrails/ and the change's own openspec/changes/<change>/ are excluded
deriveChange.emptyChangeSet: node fails with error code empty_change_set before any provider call
deriveChange.derivationArtifact: <backlogRoot>/.specrails/pipeline/<runId>/agent-workflow/artifacts/<scope-node digest>/derivation.json; the absolute path is output.derivationPath and the report is output.derivation
deriveChange.verificationProposals: output.structured.verification (at most 20, architect schema); bind them with verify additionalCommandsFrom: <derive node id>
deriveChange.reviewer: A reviewer role-turn in the same run receives derivation.json; every unexplained file is an issue
deriveChange.correctionLoop: role-turn stance 'fixer' (write roles only; the built-in developer takes the FIXER instructions, rolePrompts.fixer and config.fixer in a fresh session). flow-spec routes a rejected review or a failing check to at most correctionLimit (2) rounds of fix then derive (feedback) then check then review; a fixer turn that leaves $outputs.fix.candidateHash equal to $outputs.check.candidateHash, or a spent budget, ends at end node changes-requested with reason 'Flow → Spec: the reviewer requested changes that <n> correction round(s) did not resolve. Latest findings: <findings>'

workflowAgentSteps.ownership: Host-defined roles, schemas and gates; Core provides scoped artifact contracts and verified candidate guards

sessions.transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdio; one host per scope
sessions.interruptDelivery: session.send delivery 'interrupt' cuts the running turn (turn.completed status 'interrupted', partial text kept) and runs the input as the next turn, ahead of inputs queued before it; on an idle session it behaves like 'queue'. Drivers declare capabilities.interrupt 'native' (provider primitive) or 'emulated'; runtime api advertises flowSessions

execution.context: Absolute JSON file: runId, backlogRoot, backlogPath?, artifactRoot, artifactRepositoryId, repositories[{id,name,path,baseSha?,scope?}], ownership{git,backlog,worktrees:host|core}, specs[{id,title,description,repositoryIds?,acceptanceCriteria?}]. scope (runtime capability repositoryScope) lists the checkout-relative directories a repository is confined to — a package registered inside a larger checkout: commands without cwd run in the first one, model-proposed checks stay inside it, edits outside it are undone after each developer/fixer turn and reviews judge the git change set against the run base.
execution.verification: Successful argv-based commands captured by the runtime, bound to frozen scope, candidate files and relevant execution environment. Unknown or stale evidence cannot pass archive.
execution.hostOwnership: Host worktrees are used directly; host git/backlog are not mutated by Core delivery.
execution.acceptance: acceptance --request JSON records every exact frozen requirement, evidence, exception authority, check scope/limitations and findings. Required by reviewer done/archive-check; bound to scope, candidate and design.
execution.completion: status.completion separates implementation, validation (verified|with-exceptions|pending|blocked), archive and delivery (pending-host|complete|pending); status.phases includes observed durationMs and attempts.
